Definition: probably from the same as G3823 (through the idea of oscillatory repetition); (adverbially) anew, i.e. (of place) back, (of time) once more, or (conjunctionally) furthermore or on the other hand:--again.
BiblicalUsage: Palin means again, once more, back. Jesus says He lays down His life that He might take it again, and Paul says as we said before, so say I now again, if any man preach any other gospel unto you than that ye have received, let him be accursed.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that again is the word of return in the gospel: Christ takes His life again, and the church keeps coming back to the same gospel, again and again.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
